routes.name: Special Entry Permit (PEI)
routes.summary: For travelers whose nationality needs a visa but who don't have one, or can't get one because there is no Salvadoran consulate nearby. You apply online and need prior approval from Migracion.

other: Only for nationalities that need a consular or consulted visa
Issued only with prior authorization from the head of Migracion

steps: Check if your nationality needs a visa
Create an account on the PEI site (elsalvadorpei.migracion.gob.sv)
Fill in the online form and attach documents
Pay the fee and wait for the email decision

routes.name: Visa-free entry and visa-required list
routes.summary: El Salvador sorts nationalities into Category A (no visa), B (consular visa) and C (consulted visa). Check your passport on the foreign ministry lookup or the Migracion list. Tourists already in the CA-4 region need a passport and must stay within the days given at first entry.

other: Nationals of Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua can enter with an ID or passport.
Everyone else needs a valid passport in good condition, and a visa if their country is on the visa-required list.
Foreign tourists coming from within the CA-4 region keep the stay days given by the first CA-4 country they entered.
Maximum stay days for Category A were not stated on the pages I read.

sources.label: RREE: Visas for foreigners (categories A, B, C)

routes.name: Consulted and multiple-entry visas
routes.summary: A visa is a prior permit issued by a Salvadoran embassy or consulate, or by the Migracion director general. Category B is a consular visa and Category C is a consulted visa. Migracion also lists a multiple entry non-resident visa valid 1 to 3 years and non-resident stay extensions of 1 to 90 days.

other: Official page lists the form only. Requirements, fees and processing time not confirmed. Check with Migracion (atencion.usuarios@migracion.gob.sv).

sources.label: RREE: Visas for foreigners (categories A, B, C)

stay.note: Non-resident stay extension of 1 to 90 days (form F44). Multiple visa valid 1 to 3 years (F47).

routes.name: Temporary Residence with Work Authorization
routes.summary: Temporary residence that lets you work (F3, renewal F18). A foreigner who works without the work permit commits a serious infraction. Employers must tell Migracion within 8 working days when a foreign employee stops working.

other: Official page lists the form only. Requirements, fees and processing time not confirmed. Check with Migracion (atencion.usuarios@migracion.gob.sv).

Temporary residents lose status if they are away more than 3 months in a row or 4 months in total in one year. Renew 30 days before it expires. Working or studying without the matching permit is an infraction.

routes.name: Permanent Residence (residencia definitiva)
routes.summary: Migracion lists permanent residence for miscellaneous categories (F32). Years needed and requirements not confirmed. Permanent residents must renew the card (F37).

other: Official page lists the form only. Requirements, fees and processing time not confirmed. Check with Migracion (atencion.usuarios@migracion.gob.sv).
Permanent residents can be away up to 2 years without losing status. The card can be renewed (refrenda) for 1 to 4 years at a time, filed 30 days before expiry.
Permanent residents who turn 18 in El Salvador must register separately within 6 months of their birthday.

routes.name: Freedom Visa / Freedom Passport (Adopting El Salvador)
routes.summary: A government program site called Adopting El Salvador promotes a Freedom Passport. The page needs JavaScript and no terms could be read. Treat as unconfirmed until official details are seen.

other: Official terms not readable. Eligibility, fees and what it grants are unconfirmed.

routes.name: Salvadoran nationality by descent (child of a Salvadoran parent)
routes.summary: A child of a Salvadoran father or mother has the right to Salvadoran nationality and dual nationality. No residence permit is needed first.

other: Migracion's FAQ only covers children of a Salvadoran parent. Other generations were not stated.

routes.name: CA-4 entry with ID card (Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua)
routes.summary: Citizens of Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua can enter El Salvador with a valid national ID or a valid passport. A Guatemalan ID replacement receipt does not count.

other: ID must be valid and in good condition.
Stay length was not stated on the page.
